title: Constant projective Hilbert polynomial characterizes finite locally free families
statement: Let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $n,d\geq0$ be integers, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-kun-projective]. Assume that $p:Z\to T$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented, meaning locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For $t\in T$, let $P_t$ be the Hilbert polynomial of the geometric fibre with its induced embedding: the polynomial eventually equal to the dimensions of the graded pieces of its homogeneous coordinate ring [def-sfb-projective-fibre-hilbert-polynomial]. Then $P_t=d$ for every $t\in T$ if and only if $p$ is finite locally free of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Equivalently, $p$ is finite and $p_*\mathcal O_Z$ is locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_T^{\oplus d}$. No Noetherian, reducedness, or connectedness assumption on $T$ is made. Empty bases and $d=0$ are allowed; for $d=0$ these conditions say $Z=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 02LS (lemma-characterize-finite), with morphisms.tex Tag 02KB (lemma-finite-flat); numerical input varieties.tex Tag 08AE (lemma-hilbert-polynomial-H0) and coherent.tex Tag 0B3J (lemma-coherent-support-dimension-0). The equivalence is the agent-written combination of these inputs and the existing projective Hilbert polynomial dimension theorem; see report.md.

proof.text: The displayed embedding and the quasi-compactness assumed for $p$ make $p$ projective in both projective-space conventions cited here. Hence $p$ is proper, in particular locally of finite type. Fix $t\in T$, put $k=\kappa(t)$ and $X=Z_t$. Base change of the embedding gives $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_k$: the base-change definition of projective space identifies $(T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z})\times_T\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,n\};\operatorname{Spec}k)=\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Proj}(\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_n])$ by its two projections. The affine Proj scalar-extension lemma, with $R=\mathbf Z$, $S=k$, $A=\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_n]$ and the graded isomorphism $k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A\cong k[z_0,\ldots,z_n]$, $c\otimes T_j\mapsto cz_j$, of the polynomial scalar-extension lemma, identifies this over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $\mathbf P^n_k=\operatorname{Proj}(k[z_0,\ldots,z_n])$. The closed-immersion base-change lemma applies. The projective field coordinate/Euler theorem gives a polynomial $Q_X$ equal to $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X(m))$ for every integer $m$ and to the eventual coordinate dimensions, and gives Noetherianity, quasi-compactness and coherence of $\mathcal O_X$. If $X$ is nonempty, the Hilbert dimension theorem makes $Q_X$ nonzero and invariant under $k\subseteq\overline k$, so $Q_X=P_t$. If $X$ is empty, its base change is empty and both polynomials are zero. Thus $Q_X=P_t$ in all cases.

source.place: Tag 01WF (lemma-H-projective-base-change); projective properness; varieties.tex Tags 0BEM and 08AE, as in the cited field-polynomial nodes.

proof.text: Assume $P_t=d$ for every $t$. For every nonempty residue fibre $X$, Step 1 and the Hilbert dimension theorem give $Q_X\ne0$ and $\dim X=\deg Q_X=\deg(d)=0$; here $d>0$ follows from $Q_X\ne0$. In particular, when $d=0$ no residue fibre can be nonempty. For a nonempty fibre, apply the zero-dimensional discrete-topology lemma, using its locally Noetherian hypothesis supplied by Step 1. Its singleton opens cover $X$, and quasi-compactness from Step 1 gives a finite subcover, so $|X|$ is finite. Empty fibres are finite too.

The fibre projection identifies $|Z_t|$ with $p^{-1}(t)$, so Step 2 gives finite set-theoretic fibres. As $p$ is locally of finite type by Step 1, the finite-fibre criterion says $p$ is quasi-finite at every point over each $t$. Therefore $p$ is locally quasi-finite. Apply proper plus locally quasi-finite implies finite. This is the unrestricted-base criterion, not its locally Noetherian variant.

For a nonempty residue fibre $X$, apply the zero-dimensional coherent-support vanishing theorem to $\mathcal O_X$: it is coherent by Step 1 and its support is contained in the zero-dimensional space $X$. Thus $H^i(X,\mathcal O_X)=0$ for $i>0$. At $m=0$, the twist is $\mathcal O_X$, so the Euler formula and Step 1 give $d=Q_X(0)=\dim_k\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. For an empty fibre the same equality holds because $Q_X=0$ and the section module is zero. With finiteness from Step 3 and the given flatness and local finite presentation, the definition of finite locally free degree now gives degree $d$. The finite-locally-free properties lemma consequently gives $p_*\mathcal O_Z$ locally free of rank $d$.

Conversely assume $p$ is finite locally free of degree $d$. It is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation by definition, and $\dim_{\kappa(t)}\Gamma(Z_t,\mathcal O_{Z_t})=d$. Finiteness implies quasi-finiteness, hence finite set-theoretic fibres by the quasi-finite finite-fibre criterion. The finite-fibre lemma, applied to the locally finite type map $p$, makes every $Z_t$ discrete. In a nonempty discrete space every nonempty irreducible closed subset is a singleton, and strict chains of such subsets have length zero; thus $\dim Z_t=0$. The Hilbert dimension theorem and Step 1 now give $\deg Q_{Z_t}=0$, so $Q_{Z_t}$ is constant.

For a nonempty residue fibre in Step 5, the coherent-support vanishing theorem applies to $\mathcal O_{Z_t}$ as in Step 4. Hence $Q_{Z_t}(0)=\chi(Z_t,\mathcal O_{Z_t})=\dim_{\kappa(t)}\Gamma(Z_t,\mathcal O_{Z_t})=d$. As $Q_{Z_t}$ is constant, it is the constant polynomial $d$. If $Z_t$ is empty, its section module has dimension zero, forcing $d=0$, and $Q_{Z_t}=0=d$. By Step 1, in either case the geometric fibre polynomial $P_t$ is $d$.

source.place: Tag 0B3J (lemma-coherent-support-dimension-0), combined with the fibre Euler-polynomial identity.

proof.text: For the final equivalence, finite locally free of degree $d$ implies the asserted local description of $p_*\mathcal O_Z$ by Step 4's cited properties lemma. Conversely suppose $p$ is finite and $p_*\mathcal O_Z$ is locally $\mathcal O_T^{\oplus d}$. At $t$, choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ inside a trivializing open. Since $p$ is finite, $p^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $B$ is free of rank $d$ over $A$. The affine fibre-sections formula identifies $\Gamma(Z_t,\mathcal O_{Z_t})$ with $B\otimes_A\kappa(t)=\kappa(t)^{\oplus d}$, so its dimension is $d$. Given the standing flatness and local finite presentation, the definition gives finite locally free of degree $d$.

source.place: Tag 02KB (lemma-finite-flat), affine fibre calculation and finite locally free degree.

proof.text: If $T$ is empty, existence of the map $Z\to T$ forces $Z$ empty; the pointwise degree condition and the local rank-$d$ condition are both vacuous for every $d$. For any base and $d=0$, Step 2 makes every residue fibre empty, hence $Z$ has no point: a point $z$ would lie over $p(z)$ and determine a point of that fibre. Conversely $Z=\varnothing$ has zero coordinate/Euler polynomial, is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, and its pushforward is the zero module, locally $\mathcal O_T^{\oplus0}$. These assertions are checked on affine opens by the zero algebra and its empty spectrum. Thus the zero-degree interpretation includes empty bases.

source.place: Tag 02KB (lemma-finite-flat), degree-zero and empty-base cases by the affine definitions.
